target.title: fix(agents): verify completion delivery target
target.body:
## Summary

This PR tightens ACP/subagent completion announcement delivery accounting so a completion is only counted as visibly delivered when the delivery evidence matches the requester route.

It:
- propagates outbound payload target metadata into delivery status
- validates automatic completion delivery against provider/account/channel/thread targets
- requires exact account/thread evidence for threaded origins
- preserves target metadata on failed payload outcomes for diagnostics
- keeps the current-chat generated-media compatibility path while avoiding explicit wrong-target matches

## Behavior addressed

Completion announcements can be injected through an internal/inter-session path while the original requester is a channel/thread. Broad checks such as “visible payload exists” or “message tool sent something” can count delivery as successful even when the visible delivery evidence belongs to another route.

This change makes completion delivery proof target-aware: wrong thread, missing thread, missing account, and provider mismatches no longer satisfy delivery for a concrete requester route.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: Completion delivery is only counted as visibly delivered when runtime delivery evidence matches the requester route, including concrete account/thread target. Wrong-thread message-tool evidence must be rejected; exact-thread evidence must be accepted.
- **Real setup tested**: Disposable checkout of PR branch `anyech/openclaw:fix/acp-completion-thread-delivery` under `tmp/github-open-work/real-proof-20260603T073207Z/pr-89287`. A one-off non-production runtime harness (`proof-89287.ts`, saved in the review artifact directory and disposable checkout) imported the real `src/agents/subagent-announce-delivery.ts` module and called `deliverSubagentAnnouncement` through the real announce dispatch/direct-delivery path. Synthetic session store/config/origin data used a fake Discord group/thread route; only the boundary gateway/transport deps were substituted to record and return delivery envelopes. No production Gateway/config/runtime/state or private deployment proof was used.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**: Terminal commands run in the disposable checkout were `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts` and `node --import tsx proof-89287.ts`; full command transcript is in `review/real-proof-build-20260603T073207Z/messaging/exact-commands-used.txt`.
- **Evidence after fix**: Terminal output / runtime log excerpt from `review/real-proof-build-20260603T073207Z/messaging/evidence/proof-89287.log`:

  ```json
  {
    "agentParams": {"deliver":false,"channel":"discord","to":"channel:proof-parent","threadId":"thread-proof-expected","sourceReplyDeliveryMode":"message_tool_only"},
    "wrong": {"delivered":false,"path":"direct","reason":"message_tool_delivery_missing","error":"completion agent did not use the message tool for message-tool-only delivery"},
    "correct": {"delivered":true,"path":"direct","phases":[{"phase":"direct-primary","delivered":true,"path":"direct"}]}

This exercised the repository runtime announce/direct-delivery implementation, not only an isolated matcher function.

target.title: Prevent repeated byte-triggered compactions
target.body:
## Summary

- prevent repeated byte-triggered preflight compactions for the same active transcript when a previous byte-triggered compaction did not materially reduce the transcript below the configured threshold
- record byte-triggered compaction retry state on `SessionEntry` so retries require the same threshold, the same active session file, and material new growth
- preserve token-triggered preflight compaction behavior, including token compaction taking precedence when the byte retry is suppressed

## What Problem This Solves

When `agents.defaults.compaction.maxActiveTranscriptBytes` is configured, a byte-triggered preflight compaction can legitimately leave the active successor transcript above the threshold (for example when transcript rotation preserves branch/state history). Without retry hysteresis, the next turn can immediately trigger another byte-based preflight compaction, producing a repeated compaction loop.

This patch records the post-compaction active transcript size/file/threshold for byte-triggered compactions and suppresses another byte-triggered retry for that same active transcript until it grows materially. A retry is allowed when the active file changes, the threshold changes, or the transcript grows by at least `max(1 MiB, 10%)` from the previously recorded byte size.

Token-triggered compaction remains unchanged.

## Related

Adjacent to #88188 because both involve `maxActiveTranscriptBytes` behavior, but this PR handles the opposite failure mode: byte-triggered preflight compaction firing repeatedly after a prior byte-triggered compaction leaves the active transcript above threshold.

## Real setup tested

Staged runtime validation in a clean upstream checkout on the current branch. The proof harness used a temporary session store/transcript file, called the real `runPreflightCompactionIfNeeded` runtime path, and replaced only the compaction executor with a recording stub so the trigger/skip decision still came from the production preflight guard. No production runtime or private deployment state was used for PR validation.

## Exact steps or command run after this patch

From the repository checkout:

```bash
node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check \
  src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.ts \
  src/auto-reply/reply/session-updates.ts \
  src/config/sessions/types.ts \
  src/plugins/session-entry-slot-keys.ts \
  src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.test.ts \
  src/auto-reply/reply/session-updates.test.ts

git diff --check

node scripts/test-projects.mjs \
  src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.test.ts -- --run

node scripts/test-projects.mjs \
  src/auto-reply/reply/session-updates.test.ts \
  src/auto-reply/reply/session-updates.lifecycle.test.ts -- --run

node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs \
  -p tsconfig.core.json \
  --incremental \
  --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-byteguard.tsbuildinfo
```

## Evidence

- `agent-runner-memory.test.ts`: 53 tests passed
- `session-updates.test.ts` + `session-updates.lifecycle.test.ts`: 5 tests passed
- `tsgo` core project check passed
- formatting check passed
- diff whitespace check passed

New coverage includes:

- first byte-threshold crossing still triggers preflight compaction
- same active transcript + same threshold + no material growth suppresses repeated byte-triggered compaction
- changed active session file does not suppress retry
- changed threshold does not suppress retry
- material transcript growth allows retry
- token-triggered compaction still runs when byte retry is suppressed
- rotated successor file and byte size are recorded after byte-triggered compaction
- byte-triggered metadata is persisted through `incrementCompactionCount`
- ordinary token compactions do not write byte-triggered retry metadata

## Observed result after fix

The repeated byte-trigger retry condition is blocked for the same active transcript until there is material new growth, while token-triggered compaction and legitimate byte retries remain available.

Additional staged runtime proof from `tmp/pr-95885-proof/run-preflight-compaction-proof.ts` on head `bba688c7bc9de4aa9d511591a4b1a77b7ddacb34`:

```json
{"step":"byte-trigger first preflight","compactCallsBefore":0,"compactCallsAfter":1,"compactedThisStep":true,"trigger":"transcript_bytes","currentTokenCount":124,"sessionId":"byte-session","compactionCount":1,"transcriptBytesCompactionBytes":487,"transcriptBytesCompactionThreshold":128}
{"step":"byte-trigger same transcript retry","compactCallsBefore":1,"compactCallsAfter":1,"compactedThisStep":false,"sessionId":"byte-session","compactionCount":1,"transcriptBytesCompactionBytes":487,"transcriptBytesCompactionThreshold":128}
{"step":"token-trigger still compacts","compactCallsBefore":1,"compactCallsAfter":2,"compactedThisStep":true,"trigger":"tokens","currentTokenCount":902,"sessionId":"token-session","compactionCount":1}
{"proof":"summary","totalCompactCalls":2,"triggers":["transcript_bytes","tokens"]}
```

This covers the runtime behavior ClawSweeper requested: the first byte-threshold crossing still compacts, the same active transcript/threshold retry is suppressed when there is no material growth, and token-triggered compaction still runs.


## What was not tested

- No production runtime or private deployment state was used.
- This PR does not change successor transcript pruning semantics; it only prevents immediate retry loops when a byte-triggered compaction does not materially shrink the active transcript.
- End-to-end UI notification behavior is not changed or tested here.

target.title: feat(tools/write): add append mode for agent writes
target.body:
## Summary

Revives and rebases the closed append-mode work from #75549 for the canonical data-loss issue #40001.

The `write` tool currently overwrites existing files. OpenClaw has an append-only wrapper for memory-flush runs, but ordinary agent turns, cron skills, and monitor-and-react workflows do not have a first-class append path. This PR adds a backwards-compatible optional `append: true` parameter to `write` so agents can append without synthesizing a read-concatenate-overwrite sequence.

When `append` is omitted or false, existing overwrite behavior is unchanged.

## What changed

- Adds optional `append?: boolean` handling for host/workspace and sandbox write operations.
- Preserves existing workspace/root guard behavior.
- Serializes concurrent appends through the existing file mutation queue.
- Preserves validation behavior for blank paths and invalid content.
- Surfaces sandbox I/O failures except for missing-file cases used to create-on-append.
- Honors aborted append calls before entering the mutation queue.
- Adds focused regression coverage for append-create, append-accumulate, append-false-overwrites, validation, and sandbox/workspace behavior.

## Validation

Run in an isolated checkout on current `origin/main`:

- `corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`
- `corepack pnpm exec vitest run src/agents/pi-tools.workspace-only-false.test.ts src/agents/pi-tools.create-openclaw-coding-tools.test.ts src/agents/pi-tools.read.host-tilde-expansion.test.ts src/agents/pi-tools.sandbox-mounted-paths.workspace-only.test.ts src/agents/pi-tools.params.test.ts`
  - passed: `10 files / 170 tests`
- `git diff --check`
- `corepack pnpm lint:core`
  - passed: `0 warnings / 0 errors`

## Notes

This PR intentionally keeps the API small and backwards-compatible. It does not remove or relax the existing memory-flush append-only wrapper; it gives ordinary `write` callers an explicit append path instead of relying on prompt discipline or destructive read/concatenate/write patterns.

Fixes #40001.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** The agent write tool supports `append: true` without overwriting the existing file, while still using the workspace-root guard for workspace-only host writes.
- **Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw source checkout on Linux using the actual `createHostWorkspaceWriteTool` implementation against a temporary workspace on the real filesystem.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Ran a `node --import tsx` terminal smoke that created the host workspace write tool, wrote `first line`, reran the same write tool with `append: true` for `second line`, then read the resulting file.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture from the smoke:

  ```text
  workspace: $TMPDIR/openclaw-write-append-proof-.../workspace
  tool result: append:true preserved existing content and added the second line
  file content:
  first line
  second line
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** The final file retained the original content and appended the new content in order; the append path did not truncate or replace the file.
- **What was not tested:** No live Gateway session was exercised; validation used the real tool implementation in an isolated local checkout plus targeted regression/type checks.

target.title: fix: A2A handoffs can duplicate message-tool replies
target.body:
Related: #39476
Related: #91161
Related: #93293

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users asking an agent to hand work to another session could receive duplicate visible output when the target session replied through `message(action="send")` and the waited A2A path later treated transcript bookkeeping as a fresh assistant reply.

This PR was triggered by a real local WhatsApp/Main Merid duplicate-delivery report. The private message content is intentionally not included, but the observed shape was: one correct requester-visible reply, followed by a second visible message derived from the same A2A/source-reply flow.

This is a narrow companion to #39476. It does not replace #91161's reverse `sessions_send` tool guard, and it does not change compaction replay behavior covered by #93293.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix keeps waited A2A reply extraction on model-authored assistant replies instead of transcript artifacts. It excludes inter-session input rows, raw OpenClaw delivery mirrors, projected message-tool mirrors, and Gateway-injected assistant rows before they can feed ping-pong or announce delivery.

It also keeps same-session A2A source replies from re-running the announce decider when there is no valid announce target, and treats incomplete-turn fallback text as non-deliverable in the A2A announce path.

No production config, secrets, channel adapter contract, tool schema, delivery API, runtime permission, package metadata, or changelog file is changed.

## User Impact

A2A handoffs that reply visibly through the message tool no longer turn already-delivered source replies or forwarded `sessions_send` transcript rows into a second visible message. Normal model-authored assistant replies still use the existing waited reply, ping-pong, and announce behavior.

## Evidence

Values near a unit boundary (e.g. 59m30s, 23h59m30s) were formatted incorrectly because the raw millisecond value was compared against the unit threshold before rounding. ## Why This Change Was Made `formatDuration` in `session-maintenance-warning.ts` checked `ms >= threshold` with the raw float, then rounded. A value like 3,570,000 ms is below the 3,600,000 ms hour threshold, so it fell through to the minutes branch and printed "60 minutes" after rounding. Rounding first and then checking the threshold fixes the rollover. This matches the same pattern fix applied to `format-duration.ts` in #99978. ## User Impact Session maintenance warning messages now display correct human-readable durations. "older than 60 minutes" becomes "older than 1 hour", "older than 60 seconds" becomes "older than 1 minute", and so on. ## Evidence Terminal proof showing before/after behavior for all three rollover boundaries (59.5s, 59m30s, 23h59m30s): Three regression tests cover the rollover cases: - 59,500 ms → "1 minute" (was "60 seconds") - 3,570,000 ms → "1 hour" (was "60 minutes") - 86,370,000 ms → "1 day" (was "24 hours")

target.title: fix(gateway): read usage-cost cache once per agent in sessions.usage
target.body:
Closes #100041

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves an issue where operators running the openclaw-control-ui dashboard get chronic false-positive `memory pressure: level=warning reason=rss_growth` warnings that advise restarting the gateway when nothing is wrong. On every dashboard connect/reconnect, the bootstrap RPC batch calls `sessions.usage` (default `limit=50`), which spikes gateway RSS 200-600 MiB in a single ~30s window and trips the `rss_growth` diagnostic (threshold 512 MiB). GC reclaims it immediately, so it is a transient over-allocation, not a leak.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `sessions.usage` handler loaded each visible session's summary through `loadSessionCostSummaryFromCache`, and that function unconditionally does a full `fs.readFile` + `JSON.parse` of the entire `.usage-cost-cache.json` on every call with no request-scoped memoization. At `limit=50` that is ~50 full re-parses of the whole cache per connect — the burst tracks the `limit` parameter, not on-disk store size (the reporter confirmed `limit=1` → ~19 MiB vs `limit=50` → ~450 MiB on an identical store).

The hidden-session path already avoided this by using the batched `loadSessionCostSummariesFromCache`, which reads and parses the cache at most once per agent. This change unifies the visible and hidden session paths onto that batched loader, so the cache is read once per agent regardless of `limit`. The visible path already ran in `background` refresh mode, so no refresh semantics change.

## User Impact

A routine dashboard connect no longer allocates hundreds of MiB or trips the memory-pressure alarm. Cache read/parse cost for `sessions.usage` is now O(agents) instead of O(sessions requested), and no longer grows with the `limit` request parameter.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/usage.sessions-usage.test.ts` → 36 passed. Tests updated to assert the whole cache is read once per agent (`loadSessionCostSummariesFromCache` called once) rather than once per session.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm check:test-types` → clean.
- `git diff --numstat`: net -49 prod LOC (removes the duplicate per-session load path).
- Note: one pre-existing DST test (`fills every calendar day ... spring-forward`) fails on this macOS checkout at the base commit too, unrelated to this change (timezone/`Intl` environment dependent; CI truth is Linux Node 24).

## Maintainer Validation

- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kwqd945cj8jmjdffd0j8g40t` (`jade-prawn`), exact base vs exact head with 50 real session transcripts and a ~20 MiB durable usage cache: base transient Gateway RSS growth `+1431.01 MiB`; head `+0.11 MiB`. Both RPC calls returned all 50 sessions; the head stays safely below the `512 MiB` `rss_growth` warning threshold.
- `corepack pnpm test:serial src/gateway/server-methods/usage.sessions-usage.test.ts` -> 36/36 passed.
- `corepack pnpm check:changed -- src/gateway/server-methods/usage.ts src/gateway/server-methods/usage.sessions-usage.test.ts` -> passed on the same Testbox.
- Fresh branch autoreview: no accepted or actionable findings.

target.title: fix(slack): preserve custom identity while streaming
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Slack agent replies posted with a configured display name/avatar lose that custom identity when draft or final preview updates use `chat.update`. Closes #58737. Supersedes the implementation in #93972 while preserving contributor credit for @MoerAI.

## Why This Change Was Made

Slack does not support `username`, `icon_url`, or `icon_emoji` on `chat.update`; the public method contract and current `@slack/web-api` type omit them, and the SDK maintainer confirms there is no update workaround. Slack now supports those authorship fields on `chat.startStream`.

This replacement therefore:

- forwards the configured identity through supported native stream starts;
- disables edit-based draft previews when a custom identity cannot use native streaming;
- delivers those replies once through the existing `chat.postMessage` path instead;
- converts deferred `missing_scope` stream-start failures into the existing post fallback so short replies are not lost.

## User Impact

Custom Slack agent names and avatars remain intact. Threaded/native-stream replies retain streaming UX; contexts that cannot use native streaming trade the edit preview for one correctly attributed final message.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/slack/src/streaming.test.ts extensions/slack/src/monitor/message-handler/dispatch.preview-fallback.test.ts` — 2 files, 106 tests passed.
- Blacksmith Testbox through Crabbox `tbx_01kwq9kbv377k5mhe81ghmsjja` — changed extension production/test typecheck, lint, guards, and import-cycle checks passed ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28717153797)).
- `pnpm build` and `pnpm check` passed during native prepare after rebase.
- Fresh structured autoreview accepted one deferred-start fallback finding; after the fix, the rerun reported no actionable findings.
- Official contracts checked: [`chat.update`](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/chat.update/), [`chat.startStream`](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/chat.startStream/), and [`@slack/web-api` request types](https://github.com/slackapi/node-slack-sdk/blob/f006ad409713741c5d398669c69ad98a7e090879/packages/web-api/src/types/request/chat.ts).

target.title: Prevent repeated byte-triggered compactions
target.body:
## Summary

- prevent repeated byte-triggered preflight compactions for the same active transcript when a previous byte-triggered compaction did not materially reduce the transcript below the configured threshold
- record byte-triggered compaction retry state on `SessionEntry` so retries require the same threshold, the same active session file, and material new growth
- preserve token-triggered preflight compaction behavior, including token compaction taking precedence when the byte retry is suppressed

## What Problem This Solves

When `agents.defaults.compaction.maxActiveTranscriptBytes` is configured, a byte-triggered preflight compaction can legitimately leave the active successor transcript above the threshold (for example when transcript rotation preserves branch/state history). Without retry hysteresis, the next turn can immediately trigger another byte-based preflight compaction, producing a repeated compaction loop.

This patch records the post-compaction active transcript size/file/threshold for byte-triggered compactions and suppresses another byte-triggered retry for that same active transcript until it grows materially. A retry is allowed when the active file changes, the threshold changes, or the transcript grows by at least `max(1 MiB, 10%)` from the previously recorded byte size.

Token-triggered compaction remains unchanged.

## Related

Adjacent to #88188 because both involve `maxActiveTranscriptBytes` behavior, but this PR handles the opposite failure mode: byte-triggered preflight compaction firing repeatedly after a prior byte-triggered compaction leaves the active transcript above threshold.

## Real setup tested

Staged runtime validation in a clean upstream checkout on the current branch. The proof harness used a temporary session store/transcript file, called the real `runPreflightCompactionIfNeeded` runtime path, and replaced only the compaction executor with a recording stub so the trigger/skip decision still came from the production preflight guard. No production runtime or private deployment state was used for PR validation.

## Exact steps or command run after this patch

From the repository checkout:

```bash
node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check \
  src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.ts \
  src/auto-reply/reply/session-updates.ts \
  src/config/sessions/types.ts \
  src/plugins/session-entry-slot-keys.ts \
  src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.test.ts \
  src/auto-reply/reply/session-updates.test.ts

git diff --check

node scripts/test-projects.mjs \
  src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.test.ts -- --run

node scripts/test-projects.mjs \
  src/auto-reply/reply/session-updates.test.ts \
  src/auto-reply/reply/session-updates.lifecycle.test.ts -- --run

node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs \
  -p tsconfig.core.json \
  --incremental \
  --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-byteguard.tsbuildinfo
```

## Evidence

- `agent-runner-memory.test.ts`: 53 tests passed
- `session-updates.test.ts` + `session-updates.lifecycle.test.ts`: 5 tests passed
- `tsgo` core project check passed
- formatting check passed
- diff whitespace check passed

New coverage includes:

- first byte-threshold crossing still triggers preflight compaction
- same active transcript + same threshold + no material growth suppresses repeated byte-triggered compaction
- changed active session file does not suppress retry
- changed threshold does not suppress retry
- material transcript growth allows retry
- token-triggered compaction still runs when byte retry is suppressed
- rotated successor file and byte size are recorded after byte-triggered compaction
- byte-triggered metadata is persisted through `incrementCompactionCount`
- ordinary token compactions do not write byte-triggered retry metadata

## Observed result after fix

The repeated byte-trigger retry condition is blocked for the same active transcript until there is material new growth, while token-triggered compaction and legitimate byte retries remain available.

Additional staged runtime proof from `tmp/pr-95885-proof/run-preflight-compaction-proof.ts` on head `bba688c7bc9de4aa9d511591a4b1a77b7ddacb34`:

```json
{"step":"byte-trigger first preflight","compactCallsBefore":0,"compactCallsAfter":1,"compactedThisStep":true,"trigger":"transcript_bytes","currentTokenCount":124,"sessionId":"byte-session","compactionCount":1,"transcriptBytesCompactionBytes":487,"transcriptBytesCompactionThreshold":128}
{"step":"byte-trigger same transcript retry","compactCallsBefore":1,"compactCallsAfter":1,"compactedThisStep":false,"sessionId":"byte-session","compactionCount":1,"transcriptBytesCompactionBytes":487,"transcriptBytesCompactionThreshold":128}
{"step":"token-trigger still compacts","compactCallsBefore":1,"compactCallsAfter":2,"compactedThisStep":true,"trigger":"tokens","currentTokenCount":902,"sessionId":"token-session","compactionCount":1}
{"proof":"summary","totalCompactCalls":2,"triggers":["transcript_bytes","tokens"]}
```

This covers the runtime behavior ClawSweeper requested: the first byte-threshold crossing still compacts, the same active transcript/threshold retry is suppressed when there is no material growth, and token-triggered compaction still runs.


## What was not tested

- No production runtime or private deployment state was used.
- This PR does not change successor transcript pruning semantics; it only prevents immediate retry loops when a byte-triggered compaction does not materially shrink the active transcript.
- End-to-end UI notification behavior is not changed or tested here.

target.title: feat(tools/write): add append mode for agent writes
target.body:
## Summary

Revives and rebases the closed append-mode work from #75549 for the canonical data-loss issue #40001.

The `write` tool currently overwrites existing files. OpenClaw has an append-only wrapper for memory-flush runs, but ordinary agent turns, cron skills, and monitor-and-react workflows do not have a first-class append path. This PR adds a backwards-compatible optional `append: true` parameter to `write` so agents can append without synthesizing a read-concatenate-overwrite sequence.

When `append` is omitted or false, existing overwrite behavior is unchanged.

## What changed

- Adds optional `append?: boolean` handling for host/workspace and sandbox write operations.
- Preserves existing workspace/root guard behavior.
- Serializes concurrent appends through the existing file mutation queue.
- Preserves validation behavior for blank paths and invalid content.
- Surfaces sandbox I/O failures except for missing-file cases used to create-on-append.
- Honors aborted append calls before entering the mutation queue.
- Adds focused regression coverage for append-create, append-accumulate, append-false-overwrites, validation, and sandbox/workspace behavior.

## Validation

Run in an isolated checkout on current `origin/main`:

- `corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`
- `corepack pnpm exec vitest run src/agents/pi-tools.workspace-only-false.test.ts src/agents/pi-tools.create-openclaw-coding-tools.test.ts src/agents/pi-tools.read.host-tilde-expansion.test.ts src/agents/pi-tools.sandbox-mounted-paths.workspace-only.test.ts src/agents/pi-tools.params.test.ts`
  - passed: `10 files / 170 tests`
- `git diff --check`
- `corepack pnpm lint:core`
  - passed: `0 warnings / 0 errors`

## Notes

This PR intentionally keeps the API small and backwards-compatible. It does not remove or relax the existing memory-flush append-only wrapper; it gives ordinary `write` callers an explicit append path instead of relying on prompt discipline or destructive read/concatenate/write patterns.

Fixes #40001.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** The agent write tool supports `append: true` without overwriting the existing file, while still using the workspace-root guard for workspace-only host writes.
- **Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw source checkout on Linux using the actual `createHostWorkspaceWriteTool` implementation against a temporary workspace on the real filesystem.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Ran a `node --import tsx` terminal smoke that created the host workspace write tool, wrote `first line`, reran the same write tool with `append: true` for `second line`, then read the resulting file.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture from the smoke:

  ```text
  workspace: $TMPDIR/openclaw-write-append-proof-.../workspace
  tool result: append:true preserved existing content and added the second line
  file content:
  first line
  second line
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** The final file retained the original content and appended the new content in order; the append path did not truncate or replace the file.
- **What was not tested:** No live Gateway session was exercised; validation used the real tool implementation in an isolated local checkout plus targeted regression/type checks.

target.title: fix(session-maintenance): preserve zero-valued fields in warning dedupe key
target.body:
Closes #99983

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a session-maintenance re-warning is silently suppressed after limits change between two configurations that each have a zero-valued field in a different slot position. `buildWarningContext` used `.filter(Boolean)` on the key array, which collapses numeric `0` alongside empty strings — so `pruneAfterMs=10, maxEntries=0` and `pruneAfterMs=0, maxEntries=10` both produce the same dedupe key, causing the second warning to be treated as a duplicate and never delivered.

## Why This Change Was Made

The key array has five positional slots: `[sessionKey, pruneAfterMs, maxEntries, wouldPrune, wouldCap]`. With `.filter(Boolean)`, any slot holding `0` or `""` is dropped and subsequent values shift left. This means two structurally different warnings can collapse to identical strings. The fix wraps the two numeric fields in `String()` and removes `.filter(Boolean)` — all five slots are always present, positions are stable, and `"0"` is a truthy non-empty string.

## User Impact

After this fix, a session in warn-only mode correctly receives a new warning whenever its effective maintenance limits change to include a zero-valued field — such as switching from `maxEntries=10` to `maxEntries=0` (or vice versa for `pruneAfterMs`). Previously, that re-warning was silently swallowed.

## Evidence

### Runtime delivery proof — bug reproduced on main, fix confirmed on this PR

The script below inlines both versions of the key encoder and simulates the full `warnedContexts` Map dedupe guard from `deliverSessionMaintenanceWarning`. No external dependencies. Source: `proof-99983.mjs` (runnable with `node proof-99983.mjs`).

**Collision scenario:** limits change from `{pruneAfterMs: 10, maxEntries: 0}` to `{pruneAfterMs: 0, maxEntries: 10}`. Both configs have one zero-valued field — in different positions. Under `.filter(Boolean)` both collapse to the same string; under `String()` they are distinct.

```
--------------------------------------------------------------------
  BEFORE FIX -- .filter(Boolean) on main
--------------------------------------------------------------------
  scan 1  pruneAfterMs=10 maxEntries=0   (initial warning)
    key    : "agent:abc-redacted:main|10|prune"
    result : OK WARNING DELIVERED
  scan 2  pruneAfterMs=0  maxEntries=10  (limits changed -> re-warn expected)
    key    : "agent:abc-redacted:main|10|prune"
    result : X  SUPPRESSED (duplicate key)   <-- BUG: zero dropped, slots collide
  scan 3  pruneAfterMs=0  maxEntries=10  (same limits -> suppress expected)
    key    : "agent:abc-redacted:main|10|prune"
    result : X  SUPPRESSED (duplicate key)

--------------------------------------------------------------------
  AFTER  FIX -- String() on PR #100050
--------------------------------------------------------------------
  scan 1  pruneAfterMs=10 maxEntries=0   (initial warning)
    key    : "agent:abc-redacted:main|10|0|prune|"
    result : OK WARNING DELIVERED
  scan 2  pruneAfterMs=0  maxEntries=10  (limits changed -> re-warn expected)
    key    : "agent:abc-redacted:main|0|10|prune|"
    result : OK WARNING DELIVERED            <-- FIXED: distinct keys, re-warn fires
  scan 3  pruneAfterMs=0  maxEntries=10  (same limits -> suppress expected)
    key    : "agent:abc-redacted:main|0|10|prune|"
    result : X  SUPPRESSED (duplicate key)   <-- correct dedup still works

====================================================================
  Collision proof
--------------------------------------------------------------------
  BUGGY key scan 1 : "agent:abc-redacted:main|10|prune"
  BUGGY key scan 2 : "agent:abc-redacted:main|10|prune"  <- SAME (zero dropped, slots collide)

  FIXED key scan 1 : "agent:abc-redacted:main|10|0|prune|"
  FIXED key scan 2 : "agent:abc-redacted:main|0|10|prune|"  <- DISTINCT

  Bug reproduced (scan 2 wrongly suppressed) : CONFIRMED
  Fix verified   (scan 2 delivers, scan 3 ok): CONFIRMED
====================================================================

exit:0
```

### Unit test run — all 6 pass including regression test

```
 RUN  v4.1.8 C:/tmp/openclaw-work

 ✔ |infra| src/infra/session-maintenance-warning.test.ts > deliverSessionMaintenanceWarning > forwards session context to outbound delivery 236ms
 ✔ |infra| src/infra/session-maintenance-warning.test.ts > deliverSessionMaintenanceWarning > suppresses duplicate warning contexts for the same session 1ms
 ✔ |infra| src/infra/session-maintenance-warning.test.ts > deliverSessionMaintenanceWarning > preserves zero-valued warning fields in the dedupe context 0ms
 ✔ |infra| src/infra/session-maintenance-warning.test.ts > deliverSessionMaintenanceWarning > falls back to a system event when the last target is not deliverable 0ms
 ✔ |infra| src/infra/session-maintenance-warning.test.ts > deliverSessionMaintenanceWarning > skips warning delivery in test mode 0ms
 ✔ |infra| src/infra/session-maintenance-warning.test.ts > deliverSessionMaintenanceWarning > enqueues a system event when outbound delivery fails 77ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
   Start at  00:07:02
   Duration  1.33s (transform 988ms, setup 721ms, import 21ms, tests 361ms, environment 0ms)

EXIT:0
```

The regression test `preserves zero-valued warning fields in the dedupe context` directly asserts that `pruneAfterMs: 0` encodes as `"${sessionKey}|0|10|prune|"` — not collapsed.

### Migration / stored-state note

`warnedContexts` is an in-process `Map` never written to disk or SQLite. It is cleared on process restart. No migration or upgrade compatibility action is required.

## Summary - add policy evidence for `gateway.nodes.allowCommands` and `gateway.nodes.denyCommands` entries - add `gateway.nodes.denyCommands` policy metadata and shape validation - report `policy/gateway-node-command-denied` when policy-denied node commands are not denied by OpenClaw config - document the new policy rule in the Policy CLI and plugin reference docs - classify `gateway.nodes.allowCommands.*` in policy config coverage  ## Policy syntax / evidence / finding contract  Policy syntax added by this PR:  ```jsonc {   "gateway": {     "nodes": {       "denyCommands": ["system.run"]     }   } } ```  `gateway.nodes.denyCommands` is an exact, case-sensitive deny-superset rule. An equal-or-stricter policy must include every command required by the baseline deny list. Empty or missing `denyCommands` means this rule is not active.  OpenClaw config evidence collected by policy doctor:  ```jsonc {   "gateway": {     "nodes": {       "allowCommands": ["mcp.help", "mcp.invoke", "system.run"],       "denyCommands": ["system.run"]     }   } } ```  The evidence scanner records concrete config entries as:  ```text kind=nodeAllowCommand command=system.run source=oc://openclaw.config/gateway/nodes/allowCommands/#2 kind=nodeDenyCommand  command=system.run source=oc://openclaw.config/gateway/nodes/denyCommands/#0 ```  Finding emitted when policy requires a deny but config does not provide it:  ```json {   "checkId": "policy/gateway-node-command-denied",   "severity": "error",   "message": "Gateway node command 'system.run' is denied by policy but not denied by OpenClaw config.",   "path": "openclaw config",   "ocPath": "oc://openclaw.config/gateway/nodes/denyCommands",   "target": "oc://openclaw.config/gateway/nodes/denyCommands",   "requirement": "oc://policy.jsonc/gateway/nodes/denyCommands",   "fixHint": "Add 'system.run' to gateway.nodes.denyCommands or update policy after review." } ```  The finding clears when the config deny list contains the required exact command id. `allowCommands` evidence is collected for coverage and context; this PR only enforces the policy deny-superset contract.  ## Real behavior proof  Behavior or issue addressed: Managed policy can now require privileged gateway node commands such as `system.run` to be denied in OpenClaw config via `gateway.nodes.denyCommands`. Case `satisfied-config-deny`: wrote the same policy plus `openclaw.jsonc` with `gateway.nodes.denyCommands: ["system.run"]`.  Evidence after fix: ```text CASE missing-config-deny workspace: C:\Users\giodl\AppData\Local\Temp\oc-policy-missing-config-deny-Xk9xXX openclaw.jsonc gateway.nodes: {"allowCommands":["mcp.help","mcp.invoke","system.run"]} policy.jsonc gateway.nodes.denyCommands: ["system.run"] finding.checkId: policy/gateway-node-command-denied finding.severity: error finding.message: Gateway node command 'system.run' is denied by policy but not denied by OpenClaw config. finding.ocPath: oc://openclaw.config/gateway/nodes/denyCommands finding.target: oc://openclaw.config/gateway/nodes/denyCommands finding.requirement: oc://policy.jsonc/gateway/nodes/denyCommands finding.fixHint: Add 'system.run' to gateway.nodes.denyCommands or update policy after review. target.title: test: make the local pnpm test gate green on macOS hosts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`pnpm test` could not go green on a clean macOS checkout of `main` (Linux CI green on the same SHA), which breaks the `scripts/pr prepare-run` local gate for every PR landed from a maintainer Mac (#100025). Beyond the two deterministic infra failures in the issue, full-suite runs on macOS failed 13 of 89 shards with a different subset each run.

Fixes #100025. Supersedes #100026 with fixture-layer fixes (details below).

## Why This Change Was Made

Triage of full-suite runs on a Darwin 25.5 / Node 24 host reduced every failure to one of three classes, all test-environment bugs (no production behavior was wrong):

1. **Host dependence (deterministic on macOS)**
   - macOS `os.tmpdir()` sits behind the `/var -> /private/var` symlink while production realpaths state/session/media paths. Any test that intercepts or compares fs paths by equality breaks. Fixed at the source: the shared fixture helpers (`src/test-helpers/temp-dir.ts`, `src/test-utils/openclaw-test-state.ts`, `src/test-utils/fixture-suite.ts`) now canonicalize their roots with `fs.realpath` after `mkdtemp` (identity on Linux). This fixes `backup-create` late-SQLite guard tests and all three `store.pruning.integration` repair tests without per-test patches. (The same class in the qqbot scoped-media tests was fixed independently on `main` in 7a92c473c1f while this branch was in flight; this PR rebases onto it.)
   - `exec-approvals-analysis` resolved the host `python3` (Homebrew's `python@3.x` path triggers quoting). The test now resolves from a fixture `PATH` via the existing `makeTempDir`/`makeExecutable`/`makePathEnv` helpers and asserts exact equality — also fixing Windows hosts, where the old regex broke on `python3.exe`.
   - `logs-cli` asserted a rendered timestamp that follows the host time zone (host here runs `Europe/London`, hence `+01:00`). The test now pins `withTimeZone("UTC", ...)` like its siblings.

2. **Process-spawn races under parallel-suite load**
   - The forking no-output scripts (`src/test-utils/process-tree.ts`) now emit one readiness byte on stderr after writing the pid file; both consumers (`install-policy`, `secrets/resolve`) use a rolling no-output timer that re-arms on output, so the killing silence window now starts strictly after the pid exists. Budgets raised from 150ms (lost to shell spawn latency under load) to 1s/10s.
   - `prepare-extension-package-boundary-artifacts`, `dev-tooling-safety`, and `secret-provider-integrations`: pid-file waits now require non-empty content (a reader between `open(O_CREAT)` and `write` saw an empty pid file → `parseInt("") = NaN`), sibling "delayed-fail" steps are sentinel-gated on the descendant's pid/ready file instead of a 150ms timer, and the group-kill test's step timeout leaves room for two Node boots.
   - `crabbox-wrapper` DELETE_CWD_ONCE fake: the restore-wait deadline is a fail-safe (the wrapper normally kills the child mid-loop); raised 1s → 10s so wrapper timer starvation can't make the child exit 66 before the wrapper reacts.
   - `codex run-attempt.turn-watches`: the terminal-idle delay is real-clock derived (`timeout - elapsed`), so exact equality loses a same-millisecond race under load (observed `1799999` vs `1800000`); asserted within a bounded window instead. The "times out promptly" case had a 200ms overall attempt cap that startup could eat under load — promptness is proven by the 5ms completion-idle promptError, so the cap is now generous.

3. **Cross-file leaks in shared vitest workers (`isolate: false`)**
   - `server-reload-handlers`: gateway test helpers set `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS`/`OPENCLAW_SKIP_PROVIDERS` at module load; a leaked value routes reloads into the skip branch. Added the same documented `beforeEach` guard `server-aux-handlers.test.ts` already uses.
   - `gateway run --token` exports credentials into `process.env` as a production side effect; `run.option-collisions` now snapshots/clears them (polluter side) and `run-main.exit` clears them per test (victim side) — a leaked `tok_run` changed gateway preflight auth.
   - `imessage monitor.watch-subscribe-retry`: sibling suites install the imessage runtime singleton without clearing it; a leaked runtime resurrects another file's recovery cursor and `watch.subscribe` gains an unexpected `since_rowid`. The test now clears the singleton in `beforeEach`.

**Supersedes #100026:** that PR loosens the Windows-render regex (still host-dependent), adds a second compare path to the backup spy, patches two pruning expectations, and adds a `paths.ts` realpath-parent fallback for missing files. With fixture roots canonicalized, all of those tests pass without per-test patches and without the production change, so the fixture-layer fix is preferred (`main` stays lean; no prod diff in this PR).

**Known remaining (out of scope):** `src/gateway/server-startup-log.test.ts` ("blocked channel plugin" warnings) can still flip under worker sharing — the mock on `plugin-registry` is bypassed when the dynamically imported blocker chain was cached by another file, and the real registry then sees the repo's bundled slack manifest. Deterministic repro: add `vi.resetModules()` to the file. This is the plugin-manifest/module-leak class tracked separately (nested-worktree plugin-manifest leak follow-up).

## User Impact

Maintainers can run `pnpm test` / `scripts/pr prepare-run` on macOS and get a green gate. No production code changes; test-only (+ test helpers).

## Evidence

Host: Darwin 25.5, Node 24, system TZ Europe/London.

- Issue repro before fix: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts src/infra/exec-approvals-analysis.test.ts src/infra/backup-create.test.ts` → 3 failed. After: 59/59 pass.
- All 44 test files consuming the canonicalized state helper: pass (13 shards).
- Each fixed suite verified solo green after its fix (boundary-artifacts 16/16 while the full suite was loading the machine; install-policy + secrets; logs-cli 37/37; qqbot both files; reload-handlers/codex/imessage/cli batch: 5 shards).
- Full `pnpm test`-equivalent (`node scripts/test-projects.mjs`) on this Mac, five runs: baseline failed 13/89 shards; the failing-test inventory across runs surfaced 21 distinct cases (each run samples a different subset); intermediate runs converged to 1 failed shard as fixes landed (the qqbot pair was proven pre-existing by reverse-applying the helper edits against pristine helpers, and the tooling pid-file pair surfaced only in run 4); **final run on the committed tree: 89/89 shards passed, exit 0**.
- Typecheck: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -b tsconfig.projects.json` exit 0.
- Codex autoreview (`gpt-5.5`): clean, no accepted/actionable findings.

target.title: fix: propagate gateway TLS fingerprints to bootstrap clients
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Gateway clients bootstrapped outside `callGateway` (ACP, MCP channel bridge, and native approval handling) did not receive the local TLS certificate fingerprint for a self-signed local WSS gateway.
- Why it matters: those clients could fail TLS verification even when the local gateway bootstrap had enough information to trust the generated certificate.
- What changed: added a shared TLS fingerprint resolver, reused it from `callGateway`, propagated `bootstrap.tlsFingerprint` into ACP/MCP/approval `GatewayClient` construction, and added regression coverage for local, remote, override, and non-TLS cases.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): no gateway server TLS behavior, auth mode, config schema, environment variable, or public endpoint changed.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [x] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [x] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes: N/A
- Related: N/A
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: ACP bootstrap can reach a locally configured TLS gateway using the bootstrapped local TLS fingerprint instead of failing certificate verification.
- Real environment tested: local OpenClaw checkout on Linux, temporary config/state under `/tmp/openclaw-tls-pr-smoke`, self-signed local WSS gateway on `127.0.0.1:19791`, auth disabled for the smoke.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/openclaw-tls-pr-smoke/openclaw.json \
OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-tls-pr-smoke/state \
pnpm openclaw gateway run --allow-unconfigured --port 19791 --ws-log compact

OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/openclaw-tls-pr-smoke/openclaw.json \
OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-tls-pr-smoke/state \
pnpm openclaw gateway health --url wss://127.0.0.1:19791

printf 'exit\n' | \
OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/openclaw-tls-pr-smoke/openclaw.json \
OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-tls-pr-smoke/state \
pnpm openclaw acp client --cwd /home/jet/openclaw-dev
```

- Evidence after fix (copied terminal/log output):

```text
Gateway Health
OK (27ms)

[gateway] http server listening ...
[gateway] ready
[ws] ⇄ res ✓ health ...

ACP output reached the gateway connection path and then stopped at the expected local scope approval gate:
gateway connect failed: GatewayClientRequestError: scope upgrade pending approval (requestId: 84eb4a78-9285-4ccf-8ee1-8ba98c5945a5)
ACP bridge failed: scope upgrade pending approval (requestId: 84eb4a78-9285-4ccf-8ee1-8ba98c5945a5)
```

- Observed result after fix: local TLS health succeeded, and ACP reached the gateway authorization path without a TLS/self-signed certificate or fingerprint mismatch.
- What was not tested: a full ACP prompt turn after approving the scope upgrade in the temporary local gateway.
- Before evidence (optional but encouraged): the bug was covered by the new regression tests rather than a saved failing runtime log.

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: local TLS fingerprint selection lived inside `callGateway`, while shared bootstrap resolution only returned URL/auth/timeout data. ACP, MCP channel bridge, and operator approval clients constructed `GatewayClient` without the local TLS fingerprint.
- Missing detection / guardrail: no test asserted that bootstrap clients forward a resolved TLS fingerprint into `GatewayClient`.
- Contributing context (if known): remote-mode and environment URL overrides needed explicit precedence rules so remote pins are applied only to TLS remote targets.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [x] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target test or file: `src/gateway/client-bootstrap.test.ts`, `src/acp/server.startup.test.ts`, `src/gateway/operator-approvals-client.test.ts`.
- Scenario the test should lock in: local TLS bootstrap returns and forwards the local fingerprint; explicit CLI fingerprints win; remote TLS fingerprints are inherited only for TLS remote targets; non-TLS targets do not receive TLS pins.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: it validates the shared resolver and each client construction seam without needing a long-lived gateway process.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): `src/gateway/call.test.ts` covered `callGateway` behavior only.
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Local self-signed TLS gateway clients launched through ACP, MCP channel bridge, and native approval handling now inherit the same trusted fingerprint behavior that `callGateway` already had.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
resolve bootstrap -> GatewayClient(url, token) -> local WSS cert verification can fail

After:
resolve bootstrap -> resolve TLS fingerprint -> GatewayClient(url, token, tlsFingerprint) -> local WSS trust succeeds
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`): No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`): No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`): No
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`): No
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`): No
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: N/A

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Linux local development machine
- Runtime/container: Node/pnpm local checkout
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel (if any): Gateway local WSS, ACP client smoke
- Relevant config (redacted): temporary config with `gateway.mode=local`, `gateway.tls.enabled=true`, `gateway.tls.autoGenerate=true`, `gateway.bind=loopback`, `gateway.port=19791`

### Steps

1. Start a temporary local TLS gateway with self-signed auto-generated certs.
2. Run `pnpm openclaw gateway health --url wss://127.0.0.1:19791` against that gateway.
3. Start `pnpm openclaw acp client --cwd /home/jet/openclaw-dev` against the same temporary config.
4. Run targeted gateway/ACP/MCP regression tests and changed-file checks.
5. Run Codex review against `origin/main` and address the findings.

### Expected

- Bootstrap clients receive the correct TLS fingerprint for the selected gateway target.
- Local WSS bootstrap does not fail due to the self-signed gateway certificate.
- Remote TLS pins are not applied to plain `ws://` targets or local fallback targets.

### Actual

- `gateway health` returned `OK` over local WSS.
- ACP reached the gateway authorization path and stopped at the expected scope upgrade approval gate, with no TLS/fingerprint failure.
- Targeted tests and changed-file checks passed.
- Codex review reported no remaining actionable correctness issues after two review fixes.

## Evidence

- [ ] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

Validation commands run locally:

```bash

## Summary - add policy evidence for `gateway.nodes.allowCommands` and `gateway.nodes.denyCommands` entries - add `gateway.nodes.denyCommands` policy metadata and shape validation - report `policy/gateway-node-command-denied` when policy-denied node commands are not denied by OpenClaw config - document the new policy rule in the Policy CLI and plugin reference docs - classify `gateway.nodes.allowCommands.*` in policy config coverage  ## Policy syntax / evidence / finding contract  Policy syntax added by this PR:  ```jsonc {   "gateway": {     "nodes": {       "denyCommands": ["system.run"]     }   } } ```  `gateway.nodes.denyCommands` is an exact, case-sensitive deny-superset rule. An equal-or-stricter policy must include every command required by the baseline deny list. Empty or missing `denyCommands` means this rule is not active.  OpenClaw config evidence collected by policy doctor:  ```jsonc {   "gateway": {     "nodes": {       "allowCommands": ["mcp.help", "mcp.invoke", "system.run"],       "denyCommands": ["system.run"]     }   } } ```  The evidence scanner records concrete config entries as:  ```text kind=nodeAllowCommand command=system.run source=oc://openclaw.config/gateway/nodes/allowCommands/#2 kind=nodeDenyCommand  command=system.run source=oc://openclaw.config/gateway/nodes/denyCommands/#0 ```  Finding emitted when policy requires a deny but config does not provide it:  ```json {   "checkId": "policy/gateway-node-command-denied",   "severity": "error",   "message": "Gateway node command 'system.run' is denied by policy but not denied by OpenClaw config.",   "path": "openclaw config",   "ocPath": "oc://openclaw.config/gateway/nodes/denyCommands",   "target": "oc://openclaw.config/gateway/nodes/denyCommands",   "requirement": "oc://policy.jsonc/gateway/nodes/denyCommands",   "fixHint": "Add 'system.run' to gateway.nodes.denyCommands or update policy after review." } ```  The finding clears when the config deny list contains the required exact command id. `allowCommands` evidence is collected for coverage and context; this PR only enforces the policy deny-superset contract.  ## Real behavior proof  Behavior or issue addressed: Managed policy can now require privileged gateway node commands such as `system.run` to be denied in OpenClaw config via `gateway.nodes.denyCommands`. The policy doctor reports the missing config deny and clears once the config denylist covers the policy denylist. target.title: fix: roll rounded durations into seconds
target.body:
Closes #99978

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users reading duration output could see `1000ms` when a sub-second value such as 999.6ms rounded up to the next unit boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

The duration helpers now decide whether to stay in milliseconds after calculating the rounded millisecond value, so values that round to 1000ms flow through the existing seconds formatting path. This keeps the fix limited to the shared formatter behavior and adds regression coverage for all three affected duration displays.

## User Impact

Timing text now stays in the expected unit scheme: rounded sub-second durations display as `1s` instead of the confusing `1000ms` edge case.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: `formatDurationPrecise`, `formatDurationCompact`, and `formatDurationHuman` return `1s` for 999.6ms.
- Commands / artifacts:
  - `git diff --check` passed.
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/format-time/format-time.test.ts --reporter=verbose` passed: 1 file, 60 tests.
  - `node --import tsx -e "const m=await import('./src/infra/format-time/format-duration.ts'); console.log(JSON.stringify({precise:m.formatDurationPrecise(999.6),compact:m.formatDurationCompact(999.6),human:m.formatDurationHuman(999.6)}))"` printed `{"precise":"1s","compact":"1s","human":"1s"}`.
  - `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode local` passed with no accepted/actionable findings.
- Observed result: all affected duration helpers roll rounded 1000ms values into the existing seconds display path.
- Not tested / proof gaps:
  - No broad suite or full typecheck run; this is a two-file formatter fix and the focused formatter test covers the changed behavior.
  - First focused test attempt failed because the fresh isolated worktree had no `node_modules` (`OPENCLAW_MISSING_VITEST`); `corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` completed successfully and the same focused test passed afterward.

target.title: refactor(security): consolidate secret primitives
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Secret display masking and constant-time secret comparison were split across a generic utility, plugin-local wrappers, and ad hoc forwarding helpers. That duplicated security-sensitive contracts and made exact behavior harder to audit.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Move the existing API-key display policy from `src/utils` to the security owner boundary without changing its empty, short-value, control-character, prefix/suffix, or UTF-16 code-unit behavior.
- Keep constant-time string comparison as exact padded UTF-8 byte equality, including equal-length `timingSafeEqual` inputs and explicit original-length rejection.
- Remove Browser, Voice Call, Webhooks, and Zalo forwarding wrappers so callers use the existing canonical Plugin SDK comparison export directly.
- Keep Talk Voice's one-consumer prefix display helper local instead of adding a new public Plugin SDK subpath.

## User Impact

No intended behavior change. Existing masked output remains byte-for-byte stable for covered inputs, and authentication/webhook comparisons retain exact string equality without unequal-length short-circuiting.

## Evidence

- LOC after trim: 15 files, `+87/-88` overall; production `+18/-44` (net `-26`); tests `+69/-44` (net `+25`); docs/generated/SDK contract `0`.
- Focused tests: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/security/secret-mask.test.ts src/security/secret-equal.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/server.auth-token-gates-http.test.ts extensions/voice-call/src/webhook-security.test.ts extensions/webhooks/src/http.test.ts extensions/zalo/src/monitor.webhook.test.ts` (5 shards, 74 tests).

target.title: refactor(types): remove redundant local aliases

## What Problem This Solves

Small private type aliases that only rename an existing type add vocabulary without adding narrowing, branding, ownership, or compatibility value. They make signatures harder to trace and obscure the canonical type.

## Why This Change Was Made

Audit exact identity aliases and remove 20 non-exported, one-use aliases across core and bundled plugins. Each use now names the existing canonical type directly. Exported aliases, documented Plugin SDK names, branded or narrowed types, protocol-state distinctions, generic assertion helpers, and aliases with credible independent evolution value were intentionally excluded. The shipped `ParsedGenerationModelRef` export remains intact.

## User Impact

No runtime or user-visible behavior changes. Maintainers see fewer redundant type names and can trace affected signatures directly to their canonical definitions.

- Exact diff audit: 20 removed `type LocalName = ExistingType` declarations across 20 files; 24 insertions, 55 deletions.

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Wave 3 of the shared utility consolidation found that canonical OpenClaw home-path behavior was split between `src/infra/home-dir.ts` and generic `src/utils.ts`. Resolution already had a focused owner, while `resolveUserPath` was duplicated and user-facing home presentation remained embedded in the broad utility module.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Makes `src/infra/home-dir.ts` the single owner for effective/OS home resolution and user-path expansion.
- Moves display-only home shortening into focused internal `src/infra/home-dir-display.ts`.
- Keeps `src/utils.ts` as the existing compatibility facade, preserving export identity and callers.
- Keeps terminal token-safe display, daemon/service policy, sandbox containment, config/state ownership, URL/media paths, shell expansion, and package/plugin-local contracts separate.
- Avoids expanding `openclaw/plugin-sdk/infra-runtime`; the display module is not part of an SDK barrel.

## User Impact

No intended behavior change. HOME/USERPROFILE/homedir precedence, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, `~`/`~/`/`~\\`, unsupported `~user`, blank/relative/absolute paths, separators, normalization, fallback behavior, and display prefixes remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/home-dir.test.ts src/infra/home-dir-display.test.ts src/utils.test.ts` — 3 shards, 41 tests passed on the rebased head.
- Testbox-through-Crabbox `tbx_01kwn62ve4kgj861grf9rrdcsn` / Actions run 28688257004 — `pnpm check:changed`, full `pnpm build`, plugin SDK export validation, and `pnpm check:import-cycles` passed; zero runtime value cycles.

- Live GitHub overlap search found no existing home-path/home-dir/tilde consolidation PR or issue.

target.title: fix: WebChat stop fails for WeChat channel sessions
target.body:
Related: #91987

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes WebChat `/stop` failing to stop looping channel-originated agent turns, observed with a WeChat channel session selected in WebChat.

## Why This Change Was Made

WebChat exact stop text now bypasses slash-menu selection and is submitted as the typed command, so `/stop` reliably reaches the abort path.

The gateway abort path now preserves the selected explicit channel session key across the active state used by this flow:

- `chatAbortControllers` for normal WebChat/chat runs
- hidden registered or pre-registered channel runs when the request names that explicit channel session
- `replyRunRegistry` for active channel auto-reply operations that do not have a chat abort controller

Broad `agent:main`/global stop requests no longer infer a hidden channel session. They abort only matching visible/global scope unless the request already carries the explicit channel session key.

## User Impact

Users viewing a WeChat/channel session in WebChat can stop a looping channel agent with `/stop`. Broad visible sessions still do not accidentally stop unrelated hidden channel work.

## Evidence

Video proof:

- Before fix:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1107f4e1-8450-4f2b-981a-ac5815673ed2

- After fix, selected WeChat channel session `/stop` stops the channel loop:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/25f32135-1f1a-4f9c-b0a7-ddade5464b86

- After fix, main session `/stop` does not affect the running WeChat channel session:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/969c19dd-bec6-42a4-a39f-3e526c58e045

- **Multi-channel isolation proof:** after fix, WeChat and Telegram channel sessions are both running at the same time; WebChat has the WeChat channel session selected; sending `/stop` aborts only the selected WeChat channel run, while the Telegram channel run continues unaffected. This video is the explicit proof for the multi-channel stop-isolation case.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e5b78d13-90c5-416f-a354-610fef9b6c59

Redacted terminal/log proof from a local PR-head build:

How to read this proof:

- The first block is WebChat with the WeChat channel session selected. The UI sends `chat.abort` for the explicit WeChat session key, and Gateway aborts the matching `replyRunRegistry` operation.
- The second block is WebChat with the main session selected while the WeChat channel run is still active. The UI sends `chat.abort` for `agent:main:main`; Gateway returns `aborted=false runIds=[]`, and the same WeChat run continues afterward.
- The multi-channel isolation video proof is a separate stronger case: WeChat and Telegram channel runs are active at the same time, selected WeChat `/stop` aborts only WeChat, and Telegram continues unaffected.

```text
[positive: WebChat selected WeChat channel session and submitted /stop]
00:27:03 WebChat UI stop command:
  message="/stop"
  selectedWebChatSessionKey="agent:main:openclaw-weixin:direct:<wechat-user>@im.wechat"
  chatRunId=null

00:27:03 Gateway chat.abort request from WebChat:
  sessionKey="agent:main:openclaw-weixin:direct:<wechat-user>@im.wechat"
  rawSessionKey="agent:main:openclaw-weixin:direct:<wechat-user>@im.wechat"
  aliases=[]
  agentId=null
  requesterAdmin=true

00:27:03 Gateway abort match:
  origin=rpc
  sessionKeys=["agent:main:openclaw-weixin:direct:<wechat-user>@im.wechat"]
  matchedActive=0
  authorizedActive=0
  matchedPending=0
  authorizedPending=0
  replyRunKeys=["agent:main:openclaw-weixin:direct:<wechat-user>@im.wechat"]

00:27:03 Gateway chat.abort response to WebChat:
  sessionKey="agent:main:openclaw-weixin:direct:<wechat-user>@im.wechat"
  aborted=true
  runIds=["reply:agent:main:openclaw-weixin:direct:<wechat-user>@im.wechat"]
  unauthorized=false

[negative: WebChat selected main session and submitted /stop while WeChat run was active]
00:30:42 openclaw-weixin channel run was active immediately before main-session /stop:
  runId=<wechat-run>
  tool=exec

00:30:43 WebChat UI stop command from main session:
  message="/stop"
  selectedWebChatSessionKey="agent:main:main"
  chatRunId=null

00:30:43 Gateway chat.abort request from WebChat main session:
  sessionKey="agent:main:main"
  rawSessionKey="agent:main:main"
  aliases=[]
  agentId="main"
  requesterAdmin=true

00:30:43 Gateway chat.abort response to WebChat main session:
  sessionKey="agent:main:main"
  aborted=false
  runIds=[]
  unauthorized=false

00:30:44 openclaw-weixin continued the same channel run after main-session /stop:
  embedded run tool start runId=<wechat-run> tool=exec

00:30:46 openclaw-weixin continued:
  embedded run tool start runId=<wechat-run> tool=exec

00:30:55 heartbeat after main-session /stop:
  active=1

00:31:10 openclaw-weixin continued:
  embedded run tool start runId=<wechat-run> tool=exec
```

- Manual local proof: rebuilt gateway/Control UI, restarted local gateway, reproduced WeChat channel loop, and confirmed WebChat `/stop` stopped the running turn.
- Manual local negative proof: rebuilt gateway/Control UI, restarted local gateway, started a WeChat channel run, sent `/stop` from the main session, and confirmed the WeChat channel run continued.
- Manual local multi-channel isolation proof: rebuilt gateway/Control UI, restarted local gateway, ran WeChat and Telegram channel tasks concurrently, sent `/stop` from the selected WeChat channel session, and confirmed Telegram continued unaffected.

## What Problem This Solves

Portable agent tool-result construction was duplicated across multiple plugins. Exact pretty-JSON result builders repeatedly recreated the same contract: one text block containing `JSON.stringify(payload, null, 2)` plus the same typed payload in `details`.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a narrow `openclaw/plugin-sdk/tool-results` entrypoint that exposes the canonical typed `textResult` and `jsonResult` helpers, then migrates only callers with identical contracts. MCP structured/error results, browser sanitization, media/file results, approvals, channel presentation, transport envelopes, and caller-specific failure semantics remain with their existing owners.

The consolidation removes local constructors and one duplicate result type while preserving the existing model-facing text and structured details behavior.

## User Impact

No intended behavior change. Plugin tools keep returning the same text and `details` payloads. Plugin authors gain a small supported SDK seam for portable text and pretty-JSON agent results.

### SDK surface metric and merge risk

- Public entrypoints: **+1** (`323 -> 324`)
- Public exports: **+3** (`10,425 -> 10,428`)
- Public callable exports: **+2** (`5,237 -> 5,239`)

This is an additive public SDK contract, so the matching package export, API metadata/checksum, docs, and exact surface-budget ceilings are updated together. The merge risk is limited to that additive surface; no existing SDK entrypoint is removed or changed, and migrated runtime shapes are unchanged.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs --check`
  - Public SDK totals: 324 entrypoints, 10,428 exports, 5,239 callable exports.
- `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check`

target.title: fix(agent-core): resolve tool-name mismatches for Claude Code alias calls
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agents trained on Claude Code emit tool names such as `KnowledgeSearch`, `Glob`, and `Grep`. These names don't exist in a stock OpenClaw runtime, producing `Tool X not found` errors and causing the model to retry the same call until it gives up.

LCM corpus analysis on a private deployment (2026-03-15 – 2026-07-01):

| Tool name called | Failures |
|---|---|
| KnowledgeSearch | 2,586 |
| Glob | 1,234 |
| Grep | 159 |
| **Total covered by this PR** | **3,979 across ~1,400 conversations** |
| Agent (not covered — see below) | 429 |

Representative failure trace (redacted):
```
tool_call   toolCallId=[redacted]  toolName=Glob  arguments={"pattern":"[redacted]"}
tool_result toolCallId=[redacted]  toolName=Glob  isError=true
            content=[{"type":"text","text":"Tool Glob not found"}]
```
The model retried twice more with the same tool name, got the same error, and gave up.

## Fix

Add `resolveToolAlias()` before the deferred-tool resolver in `resolveToolCallTool()`:

1. **Case-insensitive exact match** — catches capitalisation drift (e.g. `READ` → `Read`).
2. **Normalised alias map** — strips non-alphanumeric characters, then tries ordered fallback names:
   - `KnowledgeSearch` → `memory_search`, `knowledge_search`, `wiki_search`, `search`
   - `Glob` → `find`
   - `Grep` → `grep`

The alias table is intentionally scoped to tools with **argument-compatible schemas** — a single query/pattern string. That's why `Agent`/`Task` are **not** in this PR: Claude Code emits `Agent(prompt="...")` but `sessions_spawn` takes `task`, and rewriting arguments belongs in the deployment's own tool catalog (where full schema context lives), not in a shared alias table. Deployments that want the Agent alias can bind it themselves with the correct arg translation — this PR gets 92% of the failure class right without coupling the resolver to any one tool's schema.

The deferred-tool resolver path is also alias-aware: when `resolveDeferredTool()` materialises a tool under its canonical name (e.g. `memory_search`) for an alias call (e.g. `KnowledgeSearch`), the dispatcher now accepts that as a valid resolution instead of throwing on the name mismatch — while still rejecting resolvers that return genuinely unrelated names.

When no alias matches, the not-found error now lists the agent's available tool names, which helps both the model self-correct and operators diagnose missing tool registrations.

The original tool-call name is preserved in the trajectory and tool-result audit identity so sessions are replay-identical to the pre-fix behaviour, except the call succeeds instead of erroring. Replay is deterministic because alias resolution is a pure function of the requested name and the agent's tool context.

## Tests

Six tests in the deferred-tool hydration suite (`agent-loop.test.ts`), 22/22 passing:

- `KnowledgeSearch` dispatches to `memory_search` (alias case).
- Case-insensitive lookup (`FIND` → `find`).
- Not-found error includes available tool list.
- `Agent` with a `sessions_spawn` tool present still returns not-found (regression against premature Agent alias).
- Deferred-tool resolver returning an alias-equivalent name (`memory_search` for `KnowledgeSearch`) is accepted and dispatched.
- Deferred-tool resolver returning an unrelated name (`not_related` for `KnowledgeSearch`) is still rejected.

Local: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop.test.ts` → 22 passed.

## Evidence

**Before (pre-patch):** 3,979 `Tool * not found` failures across the three aliases covered by this PR (LCM analysis, full corpus 2026-03-15 – 2026-07-01) — see the table above. An additional 429 Agent failures are documented but intentionally out of scope for the reasons stated in the Fix section.

**After (post-patch):** the fix has been running as a local dist patch on a private OpenClaw deployment since 2026-07-02T14:43 (updated 2026-07-02T23:45Z to match this PR's head, including canonical dispatch identity). The `promptAppend` mitigation that previously steered models toward native tool names — flagged in the last review as suppressing organic alias calls — was **removed** at 2026-07-02T23:45Z and the gateway restarted, restoring natural model behaviour.

### Post-fix positive trace (2026-07-03)

~1 hour after the mitigation was lifted, the embedded memory-search subagent organically emitted a Claude Code alias call in a real production turn, and it dispatched through the resolver (redacted; source is the deployment's lossless message store — embedded subagents persist no session `.jsonl`, so tool calls are recorded there as message parts):

```
conversation: active-memory-[redacted]   (embedded memory-search subagent, live fleet traffic)

2026-07-03T00:46:07Z  assistant  tool_use     toolCallId=toolu_01Pn[redacted]
                                 toolName=KnowledgeSearch
                                 arguments={"query":"[redacted]"}
2026-07-03T00:46:07Z  tool       tool_result  toolCallId=toolu_01Pn[redacted]
                                 toolName=memory_search   isError=false
                                 content={"results":[{"path":"[redacted]","startLine":15,
                                 "endLine":18,"score":0.96,"snippet":"[redacted]",
                                 "source":"memory","corpus":"memory"}, …]}
```

Two properties, both matching this PR's documented behaviour:

1. **The alias call dispatched to the canonical tool and returned real results.** Pre-patch, the identical call shape produced `Tool KnowledgeSearch not found` and model retries (see the corpus above; last such failures 2026-07-01, 12 that day).
2. **The identity split is exactly as documented:** the assistant `tool_use` retains the raw model-emitted name (`KnowledgeSearch`) for trajectory replay, while the `tool_result` carries the canonical `toolName` (`memory_search`) under the **same** `toolCallId`.

Corroborating rate evidence from the same store: `Tool KnowledgeSearch not found` occurred 10–46×/day every day through 2026-07-01 and drops to zero from 2026-07-02 when the patch went live — while alias *emissions* continue — i.e. the fix, not a disappearance of traffic, removed the failures.

Deployment note for reviewers: the private deployment additionally binds the `Agent`/`Task` alias in its own layer with argument translation — exactly the deployment-side binding this PR's Fix section describes as the intended home for schema-translating aliases. The trace above exercises the shared `KnowledgeSearch` alias path that this PR adds.

### Known limitation (accepted scope, follow-up PR planned)

`resolveToolSearchCatalogTool` (embedded hidden-catalog hydration, `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`) still exact-matches raw model names, so hidden catalog tools do not alias-resolve. This PR intentionally covers the direct context-tools path and the stubbed deferred-resolver path only — "direct-tools-only coverage" per the review's maintainer options — to keep the diff surgical. The alias-aware catalog hydration pass is a scoped follow-up.

## Redactions

Chat IDs, topic IDs, tool call IDs (kept as stable partial prefixes where identity continuity matters), agent identifiers, task content, search query text, memory snippet content, session keys, file paths under the private deployment.
